name: Chak Angouba
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a pan until it smokes slightly.
2. Add chopped onions and green chilies, sautéing until golden brown.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for a minute.
4. Add cubed potatoes, carrots, and peas; sauté until the vegetables are tender.
5. Stir in turmeric powder and salt.
6. Add the cooked rice and toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
7. Stir-fry on high heat for 3-4 minutes to ensure the rice is hot and slightly toasted.
8. Garnish with chopped spring onions and serve hot.
description: Chak Angouba is the Manipuri version of fried rice. It is a humble, comforting dish commonly eaten in households to utilize leftover rice, reflecting the resourceful and simple culinary traditions of the Meitei people.
